neighbours.label: 'listen' / 'listening' in the sense of attentively attending to what another person says (listening as an interpersonal skill); speaking, hearing, reading, and listening to music are quiet
fire: A good counsellor knows that the aim of listening is to make the client feel understood.
Empathic listening is a style of listening that puts the speaker's feelings first.
Before you answer, take a moment to really listen to what your partner is telling you.
The workshop teaches parents that listening to a child without interrupting builds trust.
Doctors who listen carefully to their patients make fewer mistakes in diagnosis.
She believes that the secret of friendship is listening to others with your full attention.
In a negotiation you learn more when you listen to the other side than when you argue.
The mediator reminded them that true listening means trying to understand, not waiting to reply.
quiet: A good counsellor knows that the aim of questioning is to make the client think aloud.
Persuasive speaking is a style of speaking that puts the audience's feelings first.
Before you answer, take a moment to really think about what your partner is asking for.
The workshop teaches parents that reading to a child without hurrying builds vocabulary.
Doctors who write carefully to their patients make fewer mistakes in prescribing.
She spent the whole afternoon listening to old records on her grandfather's gramophone.
In a negotiation you gain more when you speak to the other side than when you stay silent.
From the cellar he heard the rain drumming on the roof and a door banging in the wind.
